paragraphs: The Peace Arch stands directly on the border between Canada and the United States, half in each country, with an unlocked gate inside it. It was built to mark a boundary that had gone unfortified for a century, and the whole point of the monument is that it does not stop anyone.
The model holds 67,403 polygons and 69,668 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $69 it suits architectural and landmark visualisation, news and documentary graphics, tourism imagery, education material, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2023.

A resectoscope works through a natural opening, which is why the instrument is a tube rather than a blade. Optics, irrigation and a cutting electrode all travel down the same shaft, and the entire procedure happens on a screen at the far end of it.

The model is very light at 12,325 polygons and 12,148 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, so it runs in interactive and browser based material. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $69 it suits medical device marketing, surgical education and training, patient explanation material, technical documentation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

Search and rescue direction finding is the difference between a search area of ten square miles and one of ten. It reads the bearing of a distress beacon or a radio call, and on a moving aircraft or vessel a series of those bearings becomes a position.

The model is light at 47,211 polygons and 48,920 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 7 maps all at 4096x4096, supplied with the antenna. It carries StemCell certification.
At $69 it suits search and rescue visualisation, aviation and maritime equipment marketing, control and cockpit scenes, training material and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

A robotic wrapper walks around the pallet instead of spinning it, which means it can wrap loads that are too heavy, too tall or too unstable to be turned. The film is stretched as it goes on, and that tension is what actually holds the load together.
The model holds 84,384 polygons and 87,281 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $69 it suits warehouse and logistics visualisation, packaging equipment marketing, training material, industrial scenes, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2021.

Cutting a vessel open is the only way to show why arteries and veins behave so differently. The wall thickness, the layers and the valves are all invisible from outside, and every explanation of blood pressure eventually comes back to that cross section.
The model is supplied in cross section, in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and is built to CheckMate specification. A second build is offered separately.
At $59 it suits medical education and patient explanation, cardiovascular and pharmaceutical material, biology teaching, technical documentation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Erecting a flat carton, filling it and closing it is three separate mechanisms working in sequence, and the machine only works if all three keep pace. The yellow guarding around it is not decoration: it is the colour safety standards ask for.
The model holds 229,466 polygons and 116,759 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in yellow. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $59 it suits packaging and manufacturing visualisation, equipment marketing, production line scenes, training material, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2023.

Flow wrapping is the reason almost everything in a supermarket is sealed in a tube of film with a crimp at each end. The product travels in a straight line while the film forms around it, which is faster than any process that has to stop and start.
The model holds 242,449 polygons and 252,175 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits packaging and food industry visualisation, equipment marketing, production line scenes, training material, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

The Avenger is a turret of short range missiles bolted onto a light vehicle, and that is the whole idea: air defence that keeps up with the units it is protecting rather than being emplaced behind them.

The model holds 77,434 polygons and 78,875 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 13 maps, 11 at 4096x4096 and 2 at 1024x1024. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $59 it suits defence visualisation and presentation, documentary and news graphics, simulation, film props, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2017.

The chunky sneaker took an aesthetic that had been considered a mistake for two decades and sold it back at luxury prices. Stacked soles, deliberately oversized proportions and a silhouette designed to be recognised from across a street.

The model is light at 30,915 polygons and 32,339 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in white, which is enough for close product work. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $59 it suits footwear and fashion visualisation, e-commerce and catalogue imagery, advertising, character accessories and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

Airsoft protective gear looks military and is engineered for something else entirely: stopping a plastic pellet at close range, particularly at the eyes and teeth. The mesh mask exists because goggles fog and a player who cannot see stops playing.
The model holds 108,178 polygons and 54,027 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in black, and carries StemCell certification. Camouflage and khaki builds are offered separately.
At $59 it suits sports and recreation visualisation, equipment and retail imagery, character accessories, game assets, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

A glove that can be posed is worth more than one that cannot, because the shape changes completely between a closed fist and an open hand. Everything about how the leather creases follows from what the hand inside it is doing.

The model is very light at 8,264 polygons and 8,216 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 2 maps at 4096x4096, and comes rigged. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and native rigged builds for Maya and Cinema 4D are offered separately.
At $59 it suits sports visualisation and broadcast graphics, equipment and retail imagery, character accessories, animation, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.

Changing a gas canister is a two second operation that everybody has to be shown once. An animated version explains it better than any instruction sheet, because the whole difficulty is in the order of the movements rather than in the parts.
This is supplied animated, in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, showing the canister replacement sequence. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits product instruction and safety material, outdoor equipment marketing, e-commerce and explainer video work, training content and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The front of a car is where the hardest engineering compromises live. Steering, suspension, braking and crash structure all occupy the same space, and every one of them wants the others to move somewhere else.
The model holds 68,841 polygons and 73,299 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, showing the front chassis together with its suspension. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits automotive engineering visualisation, technical and training material, parts and aftermarket presentation, education, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

Suspension has one job that sounds simple and is not: keep the tyre on the road while the body stays level. Every layout ever built is a different set of answers about which of those two to sacrifice when the ground gets difficult.
The model holds 69,474 polygons and 37,066 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, showing the suspension assembly on its own. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $59 it suits automotive engineering visualisation, technical and training material, parts catalogues, aftermarket marketing, education and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.
